title: Spørre om, forklare og bekrefte veien — ask for, give, and confirm directions
goal: Ask for a route, give short direction steps, and confirm that the route is understood.

objectives.statement: Ask for a route, give short direction steps, and confirm that the route is understood.

spans.value: Maya has recently moved to Bergen. She is meeting a friend at the public library, but her phone has run out of battery. Near the railway station, she asks a passer-by, Henrik, for help.
Unnskyld, hvordan kommer jeg meg til biblioteket?

blocks.translation: Excuse me, how do I get to the library?

spans.value: Biblioteket? Det er ikke langt herfra.

blocks.translation: The library? It isn’t far from here.
Great. Can you explain the way?

spans.value: Ja. Gå rett fram til lyskrysset. Ta til venstre, og fortsett forbi hotellet.

blocks.translation: Yes. Go straight ahead to the traffic lights. Turn left, and continue past the hotel.

spans.value: Ja, det stemmer. Etter hotellet krysser du gata. Biblioteket ligger på høyre side.

blocks.translation: Yes, that’s right. After the hotel, cross the street. The library is on the right-hand side.

spans.value: Så jeg går rett fram, tar til venstre ved lyskrysset og går forbi hotellet. Deretter krysser jeg gata.

blocks.translation: So I go straight ahead, turn left at the traffic lights, and go past the hotel. Then I cross the street.

spans.value: Helt riktig. Du ser biblioteket med en gang.

blocks.translation: Exactly right. You’ll see the library immediately.
Thank you very much for the help!

spans.value: Maya does three important things in this conversation. She asks for a route, checks one detail while Henrik is speaking, and finally repeats the whole route in a shorter form. Henrik gives the route as a series of small steps and confirms that Maya has understood it.

no.value: Hvordan kommer jeg meg til biblioteket?

en.value: How do I get to the library?

spans.value: You can replace the destination without changing the rest of the question:

no.value: Hvordan kommer jeg meg til stasjonen?

en.value: How do I get to the station?

no.value: Hvordan kommer jeg meg til sentrum?

en.value: How do I get to the town centre?

no.value: Hvordan kommer jeg meg til bussterminalen?

en.value: How do I get to the bus terminal?

spans.value: means “do I get to” when you are asking how to reach a place. For a beginner, it is best learned as one useful expression.
When the place is nearby, you can also ask:

en.value: Where is the pharmacy?
Do you know where the town hall is?

spans.value: These questions can produce a location rather than a complete route. If you need actual steps,
is a natural way to begin when speaking to a stranger:

no.value: Unnskyld, hvordan kommer jeg meg til museet?

en.value: Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?

no.value: Unnskyld, kan du forklare veien til havna?

en.value: Excuse me, can you explain the way to the harbour?

no.value: Hvordan kommer jeg meg til biblioteket?

en.value: How do I get to the library?

no.value: Kan du forklare veien til biblioteket?

en.value: Can you explain the way to the library?

spans.value: Checkpoint: Choose a suitable route question
Work with short situations involving a visitor, a named destination, and a nearby person who can help. Form a complete question beginning with
Henrik does not give one long, complicated explanation. He divides the route into steps:

en.value: Go straight ahead to the traffic lights.
Turn left.
Continue past the hotel.

spans.value: These directions use the command form, called the
. In route instructions, the imperative is direct but normal. It does not sound rude when someone has asked for help.

en.value: Go straight ahead.
Turn right.
Turn left.
Continue along the street.
Go past the bank.
Cross the street.
Stop at the bus stop.

spans.value: A command becomes more useful when it includes a landmark:

en.value: Go straight ahead to the church.
Turn right at the kiosk.
Cross the street after the hotel.

spans.value: The small words connecting the action to a landmark are important:

items.value: indicates the point you move toward.

en.value: Go to the traffic lights.
Turn left at the traffic lights.
Go past the traffic lights.

spans.value: Each sentence uses the same landmark, but the relationship to it changes.
Take a simple action and connect it to one landmark. For example, describe where someone should turn, how far someone should walk, or what someone should pass.
Use a small street context containing a hotel, traffic lights, a bank, and a station. Your response should contain one natural command and one landmark that clearly marks where the action happens.
A route is easier to follow when the listener can hear where one step ends and the next begins. Common sequence words are:

en.value: first
then
after that
afterwards

no.value: Først går du rett fram til rundkjøringen. Så tar du til høyre.

en.value: First, you go straight ahead to the roundabout. Then you turn right.

no.value: Gå forbi skolen. Deretter krysser du gata.

en.value: Go past the school. After that, cross the street.

spans.value: Norwegian directions often move naturally between commands and present-tense descriptions:

no.value: Gå rett fram og ta til venstre.

en.value: Go straight ahead and turn left.

no.value: Etter banken tar du til venstre.

en.value: After the bank, you turn left.

spans.value: Both forms work in a direction exchange. Commands are especially useful for short, direct steps. Present-tense forms are common when explaining how the route develops.

no.value: Gå rett fram til hotellet. Ta til venstre. Biblioteket ligger på høyre side.

en.value: Go straight ahead to the hotel. Turn left. The library is on the right-hand side.

spans.value: This is easier to follow than a long sentence containing every detail at once.
Useful expressions for the final location include:

en.value: It is on the right-hand side.
It is on the left-hand side.

no.value: Det ligger ved siden av banken.

en.value: It is next to the bank.
It is directly opposite the hotel.

spans.value: There is a useful contrast between movement and final location:

en.value: Turn right.
The pharmacy is on the right-hand side.

spans.value: for the direction of a turn. Use
to say where a place is located. The same contrast applies to the left:

en.value: Turn left.
The café is on the left-hand side.

spans.value: Use a simple map description with a starting point, two landmarks, and a destination. Write or say three short direction steps joined by
Listeners do not need to wait until the end if one step is unclear. Maya checks the turn immediately:

en.value: Left at the traffic lights?

spans.value: This is a shortened confirmation question. It repeats only the important information. Other useful checks are:

en.value: Straight ahead to the church?
Right after the bank?
Past the hotel?

spans.value: You can also use a full question:

no.value: Skal jeg ta til venstre ved lyskrysset?

en.value: Should I turn left at the traffic lights?
Should I go past the hotel?

no.value: Er det før eller etter banken?

en.value: Is it before or after the bank?

spans.value: These questions focus on route details. They do not begin a new topic; they help the speakers complete the same practical task.
The person giving directions can confirm or correct the detail:

en.value: Yes, that’s right.
Yes, exactly right.

no.value: Nei, ta til høyre, ikke til venstre.

en.value: No, turn right, not left.
Almost. Go past the bank first.

spans.value: Read or listen to a short two-step route, then repeat one key detail as a question. Focus on the turn, landmark, or order that could easily be misunderstood.
At the end of the opening dialogue, Maya summarizes:

no.value: Så jeg går rett fram, tar til venstre ved lyskrysset og går forbi hotellet. Deretter krysser jeg gata.

en.value: So I go straight ahead, turn left at the traffic lights, and go past the hotel. Then I cross the street.

spans.value: shows that the listener is checking the full route:

no.value: Så jeg går til kirken og tar til høyre?

en.value: So I go to the church and turn right?

no.value: Så først går jeg forbi skolen, og deretter krysser jeg gata?

en.value: So first I go past the school, and after that I cross the street?

spans.value: The route giver can then confirm:

en.value: Yes, that’s right.
Exactly right.

spans.value: Repeating the route is not unnecessary repetition. It gives both speakers a final chance to notice a wrong turn or missing landmark.
Create a short, guided exchange in which one person asks how to reach a named place, the other gives two or three route steps, and the first person repeats the route back beginning with
. End with confirmation or one brief correction.
Keep the route concrete and limited to familiar street landmarks. Your exchange should contain a clear request, an ordered route, a listener check, and an explicit confirmation.

en.value: How do I get to the library?

no.value: Hvordan kommer jeg meg til biblioteket?

en.value: How do I get to the library?

spans.value: Confusing a turn with a location

en.value: Turn left.

spans.value: For the location of the destination:

en.value: The library is on the left-hand side.
The hotel, the bank, the traffic lights

spans.value: does not tell the listener what to do. Connect each useful landmark to an action:

no.value: Gå forbi hotellet, og ta til høyre ved banken.

en.value: Go past the hotel, and turn right at the bank.

spans.value: Giving too much information in one step
Several short instructions are usually clearer:

no.value: Gå rett fram. Ta til venstre ved skolen. Apoteket ligger ved siden av banken.

en.value: Go straight ahead. Turn left at the school. The pharmacy is next to the bank.

spans.value: makes the confirmation clearer after the listener has repeated a route.
Maya reaches the library and meets her friend, Elias.
Ja. Jeg spurte en mann ved stasjonen.

blocks.translation: Yes. I asked a man near the station.

spans.value: Ganske enkel. Jeg gikk rett fram til lyskrysset, tok til venstre og gikk forbi hotellet. Biblioteket lå på høyre side etter at jeg krysset gata.

blocks.translation: Quite easy. I went straight ahead to the traffic lights, turned left, and went past the hotel. The library was on the right-hand side after I crossed the street.

spans.value: A little later, a visitor enters the library and asks Maya for help.
Unnskyld, hvordan kommer jeg meg til bussterminalen?

blocks.translation: Excuse me, how do I get to the bus terminal?

spans.value: Gå ut av biblioteket og ta til venstre. Kryss gata og gå forbi hotellet. Ta til høyre ved lyskrysset. Terminalen ligger ved siden av stasjonen.

blocks.translation: Leave the library and turn left. Cross the street and go past the hotel. Turn right at the traffic lights. The terminal is next to the station.

spans.value: Så jeg tar til venstre utenfor biblioteket, krysser gata, går forbi hotellet og tar til høyre ved lyskrysset?

blocks.translation: So I turn left outside the library, cross the street, go past the hotel, and turn right at the traffic lights?

spans.value: Maya now uses the same forms in a new role. Earlier she needed a route; now she can give one and confirm that another person has understood it.
Without looking back, produce a brief direction exchange. Ask politely how to reach a familiar place, give three short steps using a turn and a landmark, repeat the route beginning with
. Successful retrieval demonstrates the complete sequence: request, route, check, and confirmation.

prompt.value: You are visiting a city and need directions from the square to the hotel. Politely ask a passerby how to get there. Write one question in Norwegian.

payload.judge_prompt: Check gating criteria polite-address, names-destination, and asks-route-steps. Record taught-pattern-observation as an observation only; it never changes the pass result.

criteria.instruction: Politely addresses the stranger before asking.
Names the hotel as the destination of the requested route.
Asks for the route steps needed to reach the hotel from the square.
Observation only: note whether the response uses Hvordan kommer jeg meg til … or Kan du forklare veien til …; do not fail an otherwise successful question.

prompt.value: Put together an instruction that tells someone to turn right at the bank.

explanation.value: «Ta til høyre» uttrykker svingen, og «ved» angir landemerket der den skjer.

prompt.value: You are at the station. The route goes via the traffic lights and past the bank. The pharmacy is on the right, just after the bank. Write three short sentences giving directions.

payload.judge_prompt: Check gating criteria logical-order, accurate-landmarks, and destination-location. Record sequence-language-observation as an observation only; it never changes the pass result.

criteria.instruction: Presents three short direction sentences in a usable order from the station.
Directs the visitor to the traffic lights and then past the bank.
Locates the pharmacy on the right-hand side immediately after the bank.
Observation only: note whether words such as først, så, or deretter clarify the order; do not fail an otherwise clear route.

prompt.value: Guide: «Gå rett fram til banken. Ta til høyre etter banken.» You understood the first step, but you are not sure where to turn. Ask the guide to confirm this. Write one question in Norwegian.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate criteria isolated-detail and confirmation-question only.

criteria.instruction: Checks that the visitor should turn right after the bank; a concise question such as «Etter banken?» is sufficient.
Expresses that detail as a natural Bokmål confirmation question.

prompt.value: Write a dialogue between a visitor and a local person at the station. The visitor is going to the museum. The route goes straight ahead to the traffic lights, left at the kiosk, and past the hotel; the museum is on the right. Include a question asking the way, a short explanation, a repeat of the main directions, and a reply to the repeat.

payload.judge_prompt: Check gating criteria clear-request, ordered-route, listener-check, and explicit-ending. Record taught-check-form-observation as an observation only; it never changes the pass result.

criteria.instruction: Includes a clear request for directions to the museum.
Gives an ordered route consistent with the traffic lights, kiosk, hotel, and museum facts.
The visitor repeats the route or its key steps to check understanding.
Ends with an explicit confirmation or a brief correction in response to that check.
Observation only: note whether the listener check begins with Så; do not fail an otherwise successful route check.

prompt.value: Write a dialogue between a visitor and a local person outside the swimming pool. The visitor is going to the post office. Go straight ahead to the roundabout, turn right there, and go past the bakery. The post office is next to the bookshop. Include a polite question asking the way, short directions, a repeat of the route, and a confirmation or short correction.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate only the visible task and criteria. Accept natural Bokmål variants that convey the required route and exchange; do not require exact wording or taught phrases.

criteria.instruction: The visitor politely asks how to get to the post office.
The local person gives brief, usable directions from the swimming pool via the roundabout and past the bakery, and locates the post office next to the bookshop.
The visitor repeats the route or its key steps to check understanding.
The local person clearly confirms an accurate check-back or briefly corrects an inaccurate one.

prompt.value: What does the visitor's question mean?

options.text: Excuse me, where is the town hall?
options.why: A where-question would use Hvor ligger …, not Hvordan kommer jeg meg til …

options.text: Excuse me, is the town hall near the station?
options.why: The question names no station and asks for the way, not for a yes/no location.

options.text: Excuse me, how do I get to the town hall?
options.why: The question asks how to reach the town hall.

text.value: «Unnskyld, hvordan kommer jeg meg til rådhuset?»

prompt.value: Complete the polite question asking the way to the pharmacy.

explanation.value: «Hvordan finner jeg veien til …?» spør hvordan man kommer fram. «Hvor ligger …?» spør om stedet, og «Hva heter …?» spør etter navnet.

options.why: Til would make the hotel the endpoint instead of a landmark to pass.
Ved would tell the listener to stop by the hotel rather than walk past it.
Forbi tells the listener to continue beyond the hotel.

prompt.value: Choose the phrase that shows where the turn is in relation to the bank.

explanation.value: «Ved banken» viser at svingen skjer ved banken. «Forbi» betyr at man går forbi den, og «bak» viser til området bak den.

spans.value: «Gå rett fram til banken. Ta til venstre

text.value: «Gå rett fram til banken. Ta til venstre ___.»

prompt.value: What does the local person's reply mean?

options.text: Turn right at the kiosk; the pharmacy is on the right-hand side.
options.why: The turn matches, but the pharmacy side is wrong.

options.text: Turn right at the kiosk; the pharmacy is on the left-hand side.
options.why: The turn and the pharmacy location both match the Norwegian.

options.text: Turn left at the kiosk; the pharmacy is on the right-hand side.
options.why: This reverses both the movement and the location forms.

text.value: «Ta til høyre ved kiosken. Apoteket ligger på venstre side.»

prompt.value: Complete the sentence that tells which side the library is on.

explanation.value: «På venstre side» forteller hvor biblioteket ligger. «Til venstre» viser hvilken vei man skal svinge. «Under» og «over» passer ikke i uttrykket.

spans.value: «Ta til venstre ved torget. Biblioteket ligger

text.value: «Ta til venstre ved torget. Biblioteket ligger ___ venstre side.»

prompt.value: Which question repeats the guide's direction about the turn?

options.text: Så jeg tar til venstre før banken?
options.why: This places the turn before the bank instead of after it.

options.text: Så jeg tar til venstre etter banken?
options.why: This echoes only the guide's second step and asks whether the left turn comes after the bank.

options.text: Så jeg tar til høyre etter banken?
options.why: This reverses the turn direction the guide gave.

text.value: «Gå rett fram til banken. Sving mot venstre når du har passert banken.»

prompt.value: Complete the visitor's question that repeats the guide's second direction.

explanation.value: «Så» innleder et spørsmål som gjentar guidens andre beskjed for å få den bekreftet.

spans.value: tar jeg til venstre ved kirken?»

text.value: «Gå rett fram til kirken. Ta til venstre ved kirken.»
«___ tar jeg til venstre ved kirken?»

prompt.value: What does the local person's reply mean?

options.text: The visitor must take a different turn.
options.why: A correction would use Nei and a new instruction.

options.text: The local person is asking for the route again.
options.why: A new request would use a question such as Hvordan kommer jeg meg til …

options.text: The route the visitor repeated is correct.
options.why: Ja, det stemmer confirms the repeated route.

text.value: «Så jeg går forbi banken og tar til høyre?»

prompt.value: Complete the reply that confirms the route.

explanation.value: «Ja, helt riktig» bekrefter at ruten som ble gjentatt, stemmer. De andre alternativene avviser ruten eller avslutter samtalen.

text.value: «Gå rett fram til parken. Ta til venstre etter parken.»
«Så jeg tar til venstre etter parken?»
